newsitem.title: FRANCE: Arianespace confirms appointment of new chairman.
newsitem.headline: Arianespace confirms appointment of new chairman.

text.p: European rocket consortium Arianespace said on Tuesday its board had confirmed the appointment of Jean-Marie Luton as its new chairman.

The board, which met on Monday, had been due to name Luton to the post at the Paris air show last month but a Socialist-led French government came to power in June and raised doubts over the appointment.
Many Arianespace officials saw Luton as too close to the ousted conservative administration. Luton was previously head of the European Space Agency (ESA) since 1990.
Arianespace is controlled by French state-owned companies and organisations which hold a 65-percent share in the company. The CNES French space agency owns 32 percent.
Arianespace also reported its 1996 accounts which showed a net profit of 135 million francs, on revenues of 6.29 billion francs. It launched 10 Ariane 4 rockets last year.
It paid out 16.2 million francs in dividends for 1996.
It gave no comparison for the profit figure but said it had revenues in 1995 of 7.02 billion francs and launched 11 rockets.
The consortium operates the Ariane rocket from the ESA's Kourou launch centre in equatorial French Guiana.
ESA said in a separate statement that Antonio Rodota, an Italian, took over on Tuesday, succeeding Luton as managing director of the space agency.
Rodota, 61, has worked as the director of the space division of Italy's Alenia Spa and the British and Italian Quadratics Supercomputer World Ltd venture. He is also on the board of Arianespace.
